notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay McPherson County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The city borrowed $3,923,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Debt service leaves out $77,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the city did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to South Dakota local candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Eureka's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-20.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for South Dakota yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
